title: Pack the intact tiles and leave the broken one
instruction: pack the undamaged tiles in the box
context: Packing by hand includes a quick visual check: a broken part must not ship. The three tiles here are identical except that one is snapped in two, so the robot has to look before it packs.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Tray: a dark grey block, fixed, 14 cm (forward) x 40 cm, 3 cm tall, centred 17 cm forward on the midline. (2) Tiles: terracotta quarry tiles 5 x 5 cm and 2 cm thick, loose, lying flat on the tray in a row 17 cm forward: an intact tile (100 g) at 12 cm left, an intact tile (100 g) on the midline, and a tile broken in two along its middle at 12 cm right (two 5 x 2.3 cm halves, 50 g each, 4 mm apart, turned 3 and 2 degrees opposite ways). (3) Packing box: a beige open box, fixed, 13 x 13 cm inside, with 4 mm walls 5 cm tall on a 3 mm floor, centred 37 cm forward on the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. A piece is in the box if its centre is inside the box's walls, below their tops. 1.0: both intact tiles are in the box and neither half of the broken tile is. 0.0 otherwise: either half in the box, one intact tile only, or none. There is no partial credit: a tile picked at random is intact two times in three, so a half score would reward guessing.
reset_notes: Lay the tiles and the two halves back in their places on the tray. The tray and box are fixed (tape or putty).
fidelity: Calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The tray and box are fixed rigid boxes; the tiles and halves are rigid blocks of the stated size and mass, the halves modelling a clean break. Lighting and cameras follow the station calibration.
